title: .NET assembly reload loses GodotObject identity for objects captured by C# closures
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: Godot 4.6.2.stable.mono official.
- Reproducible in: Godot 4.7.1.stable.mono official.
- In both official versions, the MRP deterministically reports that the captured `GodotObject` has a different instance ID after every C# Build / editor assembly reload.
- The relevant managed-callable reload path is still present on current `master` at the time of writing.
- Fixed in a local 4.6.2 custom build by serializing captured `GodotObject` closure fields by `InstanceId` instead of with full-object Variant serialization.

### System information

Godot v4.7.1.stable.mono - Windows 10 (build 19045) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4060 Ti (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.6636) - AMD Ryzen 7 7700 8-Core Processor (16 threads) - 31.21 GiB memory - WASAPI (48000 Hz, Stereo/mono)

### Issue description

When a compiler-generated C# closure is kept alive by a Godot managed `Callable` and one of the closure fields directly references a `GodotObject`, Godot currently serializes that captured field through the normal Variant path using `full_objects = true` during editor assembly reload.

For `Variant::OBJECT`, `encode_variant(..., p_full_objects = true)` does not preserve object identity. It recursively serializes the object's storage properties so that a new object can later be reconstructed.

That behavior is inappropriate for a captured `GodotObject` reference during assembly reload:

- the native Godot object itself survives the C# assembly reload;
- its `ObjectID` / instance ID remains stable during the reload transaction;
- Godot already preserves C# script instances and direct `GodotObject` delegate targets by object identity;
- a closure capture semantically refers to the same existing object, not a deep copy of that object.

The minimal reproduction also demonstrates a deterministic correctness bug: after every C# Build / editor assembly reload, the closure resolves its captured `GodotObject` to a different native object identity. On official 4.6.2 and 4.7.1 this produces repeated output such as:

```text
ERROR: res://ClosureReloadRepro.cs:32 - Captured GodotObject identity changed across assembly reload: expected 1643898802383, got 1849084154453.
```

Because the callback runs every frame, this error repeats continuously after the reload.

In a larger project the same serialization path also caused the editor process to consume many gigabytes of memory during a single C# assembly reload, followed by heavy paging and an effectively frozen editor.

The editor log also showed invalid Variant serialization data during the failing reload, for example:

```text
Condition "p_size < 0" is true. Returning: ERR_INVALID_PARAMETER

System.Byte[] Godot.DelegateUtils.<TrySerializeSingleDelegate>g__VarToBytes|6_0(...)
Godot.DelegateUtils.TrySerializeSingleDelegate(...)
Godot.DelegateUtils.TrySerializeDelegate(...)
Godot.DelegateUtils.TrySerializeDelegateWithGCHandle(...)
```

and during restoration:

```text
Condition "len < 4" is true. Returning: ERR_INVALID_DATA

Godot.GD.BytesToVarWithObjects(...)
Godot.DelegateUtils.TryDeserializeSingleDelegate(...)
Godot.DelegateUtils.TryDeserializeDelegate(...)
Godot.DelegateUtils.TryDeserializeDelegateWithGCHandle(...)
```

### Root cause

`DelegateUtils.TrySerializeSingleDelegate()` detects compiler-generated closure targets and serializes each public closure field as a Variant.

The field serialization currently calls the native Variant serializer with full-object serialization enabled:

```csharp
NativeFuncs.godotsharp_var_to_bytes(var, godot_bool.True, out var varBytes);
```

For a captured object such as:

```csharp
Node capturedNode = someNode;
Action callback = () => Use(capturedNode);
```

this means the `Node` field is sent into `encode_variant(..., p_full_objects = true)`.

For `Variant::OBJECT`, the full-object branch recursively walks `PROPERTY_USAGE_STORAGE` properties and serializes their values. In real scene/UI objects this can expand into a very large object/resource graph. It also reconstructs an object by value during deserialization rather than resolving the original native object.

### Expected behavior

A directly captured `GodotObject` field should preserve reference identity across assembly reload.

A suitable representation is the object's existing instance ID:

```text
serialize:   GodotObject.GetInstanceId()
deserialize: GodotObject.InstanceFromId(id)
```

This is consistent with existing reload behavior:

- `CSharpLanguage::reload_assemblies()` stores native script owners by `ObjectID` and resolves them through `ObjectDB::get_instance()` after the managed assembly is reloaded;
- `DelegateUtils` already serializes a delegate whose target itself is a `GodotObject` using `GetInstanceId()` and restores it with `InstanceFromId()`.

In a local patch, treating direct `GodotObject` closure fields separately and round-tripping them through `InstanceId` eliminated the extreme memory growth and paging during editor assembly reload.

A runtime regression test also verifies that a serialized/deserialized closure which captures a `Node` resolves back to the same native object by comparing its instance ID.

### Steps to reproduce

A minimal deterministic correctness reproduction can use a `[Tool]` C# script so that the managed `Callable` exists in the editor process:

```csharp
using Godot;

[Tool]
public partial class ClosureReloadRepro : Node
{
    private bool _connected;

    public override void _Ready()
    {
        if (_connected)
            return;

        _connected = true;

        Label capturedLabel = GetNode<Label>("CapturedLabel");
        ulong originalInstanceId = capturedLabel.GetInstanceId();

        GetTree().ProcessFrame += () =>
        {
            if (!GodotObject.IsInstanceValid(capturedLabel))
            {
                GD.PushError("Captured label became invalid after assembly reload.");
                return;
            }

            if (capturedLabel.GetInstanceId() != originalInstanceId)
            {
                GD.PushError(
                    $"Captured GodotObject identity changed across assembly reload: " +
                    $"expected {originalInstanceId}, got {capturedLabel.GetInstanceId()}.");
            }
        };
    }
}
```

Scene:

```text
ClosureReloadRepro (Node, tool script attached)
└── CapturedLabel (Label)
```

1. Open the project with a .NET Godot editor.
2. Open the scene so the tool script is active.
3. Change the C# source in a way that triggers a rebuild (for example, edit a harmless comment or string).
4. Click **Build** so the project assembly is reloaded in the editor.
5. Observe the editor output.
6. Repeat a harmless source edit followed by **Build** if desired; the MRP reproduces on every reload.

On both official Godot 4.6.2 .NET and 4.7.1 .NET, the MRP deterministically reports that the captured `Label` no longer has the original instance ID after assembly reload, for example:

```text
ERROR: res://ClosureReloadRepro.cs:32 - Captured GodotObject identity changed across assembly reload: expected 1643898802383, got 1849084154453.
```

The error repeats continuously because the restored callback is connected to `ProcessFrame`.

With the current serializer, the captured `Label` is serialized through the full-object Variant path and reconstructed as a different object rather than preserving the reference to the existing native `Label`. For larger captured UI/resource graphs, the same recursive full-object serialization path can also become extremely expensive.

For the original real-world project, a single reload increased editor memory from about 1.5 GB to over 6 GB and then close to 20 GB, followed by substantial pagefile I/O. Disabling only the editor assembly reload immediately removed that behavior. Re-enabling assembly reload after applying the `InstanceId` patch also removed the memory spike, which isolates the problem to this closure-object serialization path rather than MSBuild itself.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

A prepared MRP is available locally at:

```text
UPSTREAM_MRP_ClosureReloadGodotObject/
├── project.godot
├── ClosureReloadRepro.csproj
├── ClosureReloadRepro.cs
└── Main.tscn
```

The scene contains the tool-script root and one captured `Label` child as shown above. The project builds with 0 warnings / 0 errors.

The MRP has been verified against official Godot 4.6.2 .NET and official Godot 4.7.1 .NET; both reproduce the identity change on every editor assembly reload. The patched local 4.6.2 build preserves the original instance ID and does not reproduce the error.

ZIP these four files (excluding `.godot/`) and attach the archive here.

[UPSTREAM_MRP_ClosureReloadGodotObject.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31141018/UPSTREAM_MRP_ClosureReloadGodotObject.zip)
